solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bruce's girl has troubles holding position up

definitions.note: Bruce is the stock name for an Australian man, and his girl is a woman in Aussie slang

indicators.note: holding says the shuffled letters wrap round the next piece
troubles works as a verb here, stirring up the letters of the little word has
in a down clue, up says the piece reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a lie is a position, as a golf ball's lie on the course

explanation.surface: An Australian man's girlfriend is having a rough time keeping her job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubles' is a verb shuffling the word before it; 'up' turns the golfer's position over, and 'holding' wraps the shuffle round it. Bruce is the stock Australian man.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheila is the Australian slang word for a woman or girl, the kind a stereotypical Bruce would court.

clue.text: Went to stop very good clock

indicators.note: to stop means to plug a gap, so this piece goes into the middle of the other

parts.note: so can mean very, as in so good, standing for the whole phrase here
went, in the coarse sense of relieving oneself, gives peed

explanation.surface: Someone moved on to halt an excellent timepiece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Went' looks like plain past tense of go; it is the slang for urinating, and 'to stop' puts it inside SO.
explanation.definitionFit: A clock is informal slang for a meter or gauge, and a speedometer is the car's speed gauge.

clue.text: Binnable appeal from examination candidate that one doesn't think to mention

definitions.text: that one doesn't think to mention

parts.note: something binnable can go in the bin, so it is disposable
a candidate unhappy with a grade asks for a re-mark of the paper

explanation.surface: A disposable plea from a student who sat an exam is not worth thinking about.
explanation.definitionFit: A casual comment dropped without reflection is something said offhand, without thinking it worth saying.

clue.text: One responsible for the death of cock fights

definitions.text: One responsible for the death of cock

parts.note: to spar is to fight, as boxers do
a row is a fight or quarrel

explanation.surface: Whoever caused a rooster's death gets into scraps.
explanation.walkthrough: The cock is Cock Robin of the nursery rhyme: 'Who killed Cock Robin? I, said the Sparrow, with my bow and arrow.'
explanation.definitionFit: In the nursery rhyme the small bird confesses to killing Cock Robin with its bow and arrow.

clue.text: To ensure present is very satisfying, produce bespoke vacuum flask right away!

definitions.text: To ensure present is very satisfying

parts.note: to make is to produce

indicators.note: right away means the letter for right is sent off, out of the flask word

parts.note: a Thermos is a brand of vacuum flask
bespoke clothes are made to fit

explanation.surface: An urgent instruction to create a custom-made flask so the gift will please.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' looks like 'immediately' but removes R from THERMOS, leaving THEMOS; 'present' means the present moment, not a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: To exploit an opportunity fully is to get the greatest value from the time you have now.

clue.text: Huge deficit in solid fuel

indicators.note: in says the shortfall sits inside the fuel word

parts.note: coal is a solid fuel
a deficit is a loss

explanation.surface: A massive shortfall in the coal trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Colossal is a synonym for enormous, from the giant statue at Rhodes.

clue.text: Quartz, say, laid underneath airline hall

indicators.note: laid underneath in a down clue puts the mineral below the airline letters

parts.note: BA is British Airways
quartz is an example of silica, silicon dioxide

explanation.surface: A quartz floor laid beneath an airline's hall.
explanation.definitionFit: A basilica was originally a Roman oblong public hall, later the model for churches.

clue.text: In flagrante delicto carpenter in noted workplace of Elvis impersonator?

parts.note: Chips is a traditional nickname for a carpenter, especially a ship's carpenter
caught in the act means caught on the hop, unprepared

explanation.surface: A carpenter caught red-handed at the famous workplace of an Elvis lookalike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noted' hints at music: Kirsty MacColl sang of 'a guy works down the chip shop swears he's Elvis'. A chip shop is a British fish-and-chips takeaway.
explanation.definitionFit: The song places its would-be Elvis behind the counter of a fried-fish takeaway.

clue.text: Batty Kelvin on Platform No 3?

indicators.note: on, in an across clue, puts the name and K after the platform letter
No 3 picks out the third letter of the word platform

parts.note: Nora Batty is a character from the British sitcom Last of the Summer Wine
K is the symbol for the kelvin, the unit of temperature

explanation.surface: A dotty man called Kelvin standing on the third platform at the station.
explanation.walkthrough: NORA BATTY is a stocking-wearing character in a long-running BBC comedy, so 'Batty' gives NORA, not 'mad'. The whole clue also describes a trainspotter.
explanation.definitionFit: Anorak is British slang for an obsessive enthusiast, the classic case being a trainspotter on a platform.

clue.text: Inquire how we may sometimes represent king

parts.note: as, as in represent something as a letter, means how we show it
K is the abbreviation for king in chess and cards

explanation.surface: A question about how a king is sometimes depicted.
explanation.definitionFit: To ask is to inquire, the plain synonym for putting a question.

clue.text: I make better hinges for emergency exit

indicators.note: hinges sit at the edges of a door, so the short word for is split round the middle piece

parts.note: I redo, meaning I improve by doing again

explanation.surface: A carpenter boasts of improving the hinges on an escape door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hinges' looks like a noun about door fittings, but it is a verb: the little word swings open round the boast.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire-resistant door is a safety door used to escape a burning building.

clue.text: Contrary reference describing bovine type not from these parts

indicators.note: contrary means turned the opposite way, so the whole piece is read backwards
describing means drawing round, so the citation wraps the animal

parts.note: to cite is to refer to
an ox is a bovine animal

explanation.surface: An opposing citation describing a foreign breed of cattle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' is used in its geometric sense of drawing a line round; 'Contrary' then turns the whole assembly over, giving CITOXE read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Something exotic is foreign, originating in a distant land.

clue.text: Painfully gratifying Pretoria party at which old girl, very fashionable, commands top position

parts.note: Pretoria is a capital of South Africa, SA
a do is a party
ma, or mother, is the old girl
so means very

indicators.note: commands means holds within, so the top place sits inside the fashion words

parts.note: chic means fashionable
1st, written IST, is the top position

explanation.surface: At a party in Pretoria a stylish mother takes charge from the head of the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commands' puts IST (1ST, the I for 1) inside SOCHIC.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes taking pleasure from pain, given or received.

clue.text: Cockchafer of gold

definitions.meaning: a dung beetle or cockchafer, a droning beetle

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is French, as in 'Côte d'Or'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a droning beetle, and in French means made of gold.

clue.text: A medic finding route back from glands

parts.note: Dr is a doctor, a medic

indicators.note: back means the path word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a lane is a route

explanation.surface: A doctor finds the way home from the glands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns LANE to ENAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Adrenal describes things of or produced by the glands sitting above the kidneys.

clue.text: Part of routine that can be a bore?

definitions.meaning: a drill is a routine, and a bit is a part
the cutting tip of a power tool bores holes

explanation.walkthrough: 'bore' looks like something dull, like a routine, but is a hole-making tool.
explanation.definitionFit: The cutting piece fitted to a power tool makes holes, and drill practice is a routine.

clue.text: N Eurasian country's sound new line, when it's pressed?

indicators.note: sound says the letter and country spoken together resemble the answer

parts.note: the letter N, spoken as en; Turkey straddles Europe and Asia

explanation.surface: The sound of a northern Eurasian nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter N spoken is 'en', so 'en Turkey' sounds like the keyboard key.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing the return button on a keyboard starts a new line of text.

clue.text: What's classified motorway entering Soap City from the East

indicators.note: entering says the road letter goes into the city
from the East means the city is read leftwards in an across clue

parts.note: Dallas was a famous TV soap opera and is a Texan city

explanation.surface: A motorway entering a soap-opera city from the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the East' turns DALLAS to SALLAD; M goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: A classified advertisement in a newspaper is a brief notice placed among the small ads.

clue.text: Country — where double agent's heart is

indicators.note: heart is says the letters sit at the centre of the agent words

explanation.surface: A spy's homeland: where his heart lies.
explanation.definitionFit: A lea is open grassland, meadow or pasture, the countryside.

clue.text: Reversible seats roughly put outside having been given a reversible brush?

definitions.text: having been given a reversible brush?

indicators.note: put outside means those letters go round the seat word
roughly says the three letters of put are rearranged
reversible says the seat word is turned back to front

parts.note: pews are church seats

explanation.surface: Seats loosely placed outside after being given a two-way sweeping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reversible' turns PEWS into SWEP; 'roughly' turns PUT into UPT, which goes 'outside' as UP...T.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair brushed upwards is styled up, a brush stroke against the usual way.

clue.text: Predictor's at cup knockout — one may be sent abroad

indicators.note: a knockout smashes the words apart, so their letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A tipster's comment at a cup knockout tie, a message for overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knockout' looks like the cup format but scrambles PREDICTORSATCUP.
explanation.definitionFit: Holidaymakers mail a scenic card home from abroad.

clue.text: Writer and manic-depressive top actor covers up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the found letters read from the bottom
covers says the letters sit inside the run of words

explanation.surface: A writer and a bipolar leading actor hide things.
explanation.walkthrough: Truman Capote was an American writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Truman Capote wrote In Cold Blood and Breakfast at Tiffany's.

clue.text: Playmaker competin' with energy

parts.note: racin', with the dropped g, means competing
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A footballer who runs the game, competing energetically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playmaker' looks like a footballer but means a dramatist: Jean Racine, French tragedian.
explanation.definitionFit: A dramatist makes plays, and Racine was the great French tragic playwright.

clue.text: Warning sound done with spirit

parts.note: a la, as in a dish done in a given style
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: An alarm raised once the drinking is over.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarum is the old word for an alarm or call to arms.

clue.text: Spooner's smashing balls on the table, requiring a bar of soap

indicators.note: Spooner's says the opening sounds of the two words change places

parts.note: pool is played with balls on a table
a whack is a smashing blow

explanation.surface: Breaking at the pool table calls for a bar of soap.
explanation.walkthrough: The Woolpack is the pub in the British TV soap Emmerdale, so 'bar of soap' is a pub, not a cake of soap.
explanation.definitionFit: The Woolpack is the village pub in Emmerdale, a long-running ITV serial.

clue.text: Reduce times getting seen in Casualty?

indicators.note: seen in says the symbol sits within the department letters

parts.note: A&E, Accident and Emergency, is the hospital casualty department
X is the multiplication sign, times

explanation.surface: Cut down the times patients wait to be seen in casualty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Casualty' is also a BBC hospital drama.
explanation.definitionFit: To axe is to cut, as in axing a budget or jobs.

clue.text: Ship with one on straight and narrow

indicators.note: on, as in on board, puts the single letter inside the ship

parts.note: a liner is a ship
a means one

explanation.surface: A ship with one passenger on board sails a straight, narrow course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'straight and narrow' looks like the path of virtue; here it describes a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Linear means in a line, long and thin.

clue.text: Direction for one loading Aussie skip

indicators.note: loading says the letter is put into the captain's name

parts.note: Ricky Ponting captained Australia's cricket team; skip means skipper
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Instructions for someone filling an Australian rubbish skip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skip' looks like a British rubbish skip, a large waste container, but is a captain: Ricky Ponting.
explanation.definitionFit: Pointing is showing the direction, as a signpost does.
